ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French AML/CFT and UBO framework: (i) Code monétaire et financier (CMF), arts. L.561-1 to L.561-50 (customer due diligence, PEP and beneficial-owner obligations, Tracfin suspicious-transaction reporting), L.562-1 et seq. (national asset-freezing); (ii) CMF arts. L.561-2-1, L.561-45 to L.561-48 and R.561-1 to R.561-23, together with Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018, governing the mandatory beneficial-owner (UBO) declaration filed with the Registre national des entreprises (RNE/INPI); (iii) EU instruments: Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD), Regulation (EU) 2015/847, and EU restrictive-measures regulations implemented by the French Ministère de l'Économie (DG Trésor).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / existence certificate of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country registry or competent tax authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract / certificate of non-conviction of the proposed legal representative (equivalent of the casier judiciaire – bulletin n°3)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal record authority in the representative's home country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Statutory screening protocol: (1) identity verification of all shareholders, the SAS President and every ultimate beneficial owner under CMF arts. L.561-5 and L.561-6; (2) determination of politically exposed person (PEP) status under CMF art. L.561-10, covering foreign and domestic prominent public functions, family members and close associates; (3) mandatory cross-checking against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (DG FISMA), the French national assets-freeze list maintained by DG Trésor, UN Security Council consolidated lists and, where the target payment rails are in USD, the OFAC SDN list; (4) independent risk-rating consistent with the French LCB-FT doctrine and the 'Low_Risk_Standard' tier assigned to the ISIC 1079 self-heating meals activity; (5) mandatory filing with Tracfin (CMF art. L.561-15) of any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) — official one-stop incorporation portal operated with the INPI; name availability and identical-token conflict checks run on the INPI national companies database (data.inpi.fr — Registre national des entreprises / RNE) and the EU business-register interconnection (e-justice).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Code de commerce arts. R.123-54 and R.123-55 and Law No. 94-665 (Toubon): the SAS dénomination sociale must be preceded or followed by the legal-form mention 'SAS'; the name must be written in Latin characters; foreign-origin words must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; the name may be in French or in another language but must not contravene public order or good morals and must not mislead the public as to the corporate object; where the activity is food manufacturing, the name must not create confusion with official bodies, regulated professions or protected emblems.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Avocat / Notaire / Huissier / Expert-comptable (regulated professional titles)
Ministère / Gouvernement / République / Préfecture / Officiel / National (state-implicative)
France / Français / Française (restricted to non-misleading identifiers)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross / Red Crescent (protected emblems)
Terms contrary to public order, public health claims ('therapeutic', 'curative') or misleading nutritional claims in the self-heating food context
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France operates no formal statutory name-reservation register: availability clearance is a pre-filing conflict analysis, and legal protection of the name accrues upon RNE/INPI registration. If the proposed name is rejected (identity conflict, prohibited token, or non-Latin transliteration), the applicant may: (1) re-file, within 5 business days, a corrected incorporation dossier on Guichet Entreprises with an amended dénomination sociale; (2) obtain and attach a written coexistence/consent letter from the holder of a conflicting registered name or trademark; (3) request written reasons from INPI within 10 business days of rejection; (4) contest the refusal before the competent Tribunal judiciaire (Paris) within two months of notification, per the administrative-litigation rules applying to INPI decisions, or seek an urgent order (référé) of the President of the Tribunal de commerce where the dispute concerns RCS registration rights. A cleared name remains actionable for a maximum of the 30-day window; no extension is available and the conflict check must be refreshed after that period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only in the 'domiciliation' form: the statutory registered office may be installed at the premises of an approved commercial domiciliation company in accordance with Code de commerce arts. L.123-11-1, L.123-11-2 and R.123-136-1 et seq. A bare virtual mailbox is not admissible for an ISIC 1079 manufacturer; DGCCRF food-business registration under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 requires a physical, inspectable production establishment in France, and the SAS must maintain identifiable French substance for accounting records, management functions and correspondence handling.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approx. 85% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by DGCCRF or the departmental directorate for population protection (DDPP) within the first 24 months of production, owing to the exothermic-reaction self-heating food technology (novel thermal processing and self-heating chemistry). Registered-office domiciliation sites are separately subject to random verification by the registrar and tax authorities, with a lower-intensity but still relevant inspection likelihood of approx. 15–25% per year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.123-1 to L.123-35 (RCS registration), L.210-1 to L.210-10 (company formation), and L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS legal regime).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des formalités des entreprises, acting with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration and Kbis issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de Société par Actions Simplifiée (articles of association), together with the declaration of conformity and the prescribed M0 formalities dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for an SAS. The articles must state the issued share capital freely, but any cash contributions above stated minimum must be deposited in a blocked French bank account until the RCS registration certificate (Kbis) is issued, after which the president may release funds. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up upon subscription and must be valued by a statutory contribution auditor unless the statutory exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a meeting of the founder(s) held at the registered office on [date], duly convened, it was unanimously resolved: 1. To subscribe for the entirety of the issued share capital as set out in the draft articles of association, each subscriber accepting the number of shares attributed therein. 2. That the registered office shall be established at [address], France, with jurisdiction assigned to the Clerk of the Commercial Court of [city]. 3. To appoint [Name] as President-General Representative and, if applicable, [Name] as Director responsible for compliance, such appointments taking effect immediately. The meeting declares these resolutions formal, binding, and sufficient for completion of registration filings with the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and signature of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and, if required, a notary; subsequently filed through the INPI Guichet Unique portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SAS statuts in French, specifying corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, issued share capital, share classes and voting rights, president appointment mechanics, and governance rules. Have all founders sign the document. If contributions in kind are present, appoint a commissaire aux apports unless the statutory dereliction applies.
required_dossiers: Duly executed articles of association
Subscribers' share subscription minutes
In-kind contribution valuation report if applicable
Power of attorney and passport of each founder if represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries missing or defective clauses, file a rectified version through the Guichet Unique and obtain a new acknowledgement of receipt; the cure period is normally 15 days after the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a French bank account and deposit of cash share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks established in France or a notary's escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name and deposit the cash share capital stated in the articles. Obtain the attestation de dépôt de capital or statutory receiver's certificate. This certificate will be included in the formation dossier and later released after Kbis issuance.
required_dossiers: Provisional articles of association
Kbis or preliminary registration proof
Corporate name reservation receipt if any
Official identification of signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays issuance, obtain an equivalent certificate from a notary or another depositary institution; for in-kind contributions, the statutory auditor's report is substituted in the filing bundle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in a legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department where the registered office is situated.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the statutory incorporation notice (avis de constitution) containing the company name, legal form, registered office, issued capital, corporate purpose, RCS commercial court jurisdiction, and president identity. Pay the publication fee and obtain the attestation de parution.
required_dossiers: Text of the incorporation notice
Payment receipt for the JAL publication
Attestation de parution issued by the legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incorrect publication text must be corrected by publishing a new notice or amending notice; the attestation must be re-filed with the formation dossier. If the chosen JAL is not approved, select an authorized publication from the administrative list and republish without re-paying formation fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the registration dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des formalités des entreprises (INPI), with verification by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M-form for SAS creation. Upload all statutory documents, including the signed statuts, attestation de parution, proof of registered office occupancy, declaration of non-conviction and filiation, beneficial owner declaration, and presidential appointment acceptance. Pay the registration fee and submit.
required_dossiers: Signed statutory articles
Attestation de dépôt de capital or notary certificate
Attestation de parution au JAL
Acte de nomination du président and acceptance letter
Declarations of non-conviction and filiation (Formulaire M0)
Justificatif de jouissance du siège social
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs
Passport copies and powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a query or refusal, respond through the Guichet Unique within the regulatory deadline. Rectify inconsistencies, re-upload corrected documents, and request human expedition if the deficiency notice is ambiguous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the RCS registration certificate and Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the registered office jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful validation, the registry assigns the SIREN and RCS number, publishes the company in the registre, and makes the official Kbis extract available. Verify all details against the formation documents and store the Kbis as proof of existence.
required_dossiers: Final validation receipt from Guichet Unique
Provisional registration number if issued
Proof of payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis contains typographic or corporate-object errors, submit a correction request to the Greffe via Infogreffe, attaching the corrected statuts and supporting board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of corporate governance books and beneficial ownership registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company management and legal counsel; filings made through the Guichet Unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the statutory corporate registers (registre des décisions sociales, registre des titres), prepare shareholder and management ledgers, and ensure the beneficial owner declaration is current. Appoint the statutory auditor if required by law or shareholder thresholds, and prepare the governance calendar for annual financial reporting.
required_dossiers: Register of securities and transfer distribution lists
Minutes and decision registers
Beneficial owner register declaration
Statutory auditor appointment letter if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any omitted mandatory corporate book is sanctioned by closure and restoration procedures before the commercial court; deficiencies in beneficial ownership filings are cured by filing a supplementary declaration through Guichet Unique without fines if voluntary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREETS / DDPP under the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty, in coordination with DREAL for environmental inspection.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Sanitary declaration or agrément sanitaire for the manufacture of self-heating shelf-stable instant meals, together with an ICPE declaration or registration authorization for the industrial production facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (Ministère de la Transition Écologique)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Food processing plant subject to the Déclaration regime under ICPE rubrique 2221 for agro-food transformation; installations processing several tons per day may shift to Enregistrement, but a full EIA report is only mandatorily triggered when specified high-capacity or geolocation thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Industrial Water Directive thresholds and local arrêté: BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L, COD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 60 mg/L, pH 6.5–8.5. Gaseous emissions of volatile organic compounds must comply with the general emission thresholds for exhaust air (typically ≤ 110 mg C/m³) under applicable ministerial orders. Hazardous reaction-agent residues must be tracked through bordereau de suivi des déchets (BSD) and disposed of at authorized facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal Commission de Sécurité or the local inspection authority after on-site inspection; structural load certification verifying floor loading for palletized inventory; workplace clearance from DREETS covering health and safety, emergency routes, and the general prevention plan required under the French Labor Code. Occupational risk assessment (DUERP) and workplace medical surveillance must be established before operations commence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) or Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE); primary portal: impots.gouv.fr. Customs and EORI matters are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) through douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS incorporated through the national one-stop business formalities portal receives a SIREN and establishment-level SIRET from the Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (INSEE). The SAS must then be registered with the competent SIE for corporate tax and VAT administration. DGFiP issues a French VAT identification number consisting of the prefix FR, a two-digit validation key, and the SIREN number. A non-established foreign entity carrying out taxable transactions in France must apply to the SIEE before or upon commencing the relevant activities, provide constitutional documents, ownership and management information, business contracts, bank details, proof of taxable activity, and a French or EU fiscal representative where legally required. An EORI number must be obtained from DGDDI for customs imports and exports. VAT registration, corporate tax registration, payroll registration, and customs registration are separate compliance processes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Subject to statutory eligibility conditions, including limits on age, ownership, workforce, turnover, and balance-sheet size, a qualifying SAS may elect temporarily for taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu), generally for a maximum period of five financial years. France has no general United States-style check-the-box election. A SAS may also elect for the VAT franchise regime only where the statutory turnover conditions are satisfied; the election does not eliminate VAT obligations for transactions outside the franchise conditions. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive apply to relevant cross-border arrangements and do not constitute a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business eligible for the domestic VAT franchise, the principal turnover threshold for supplies of goods and comparable commercial activities is EUR 85,000, subject to the applicable prior-year and current-year thresholds and statutory tolerance rules. A French-established business exceeding the applicable threshold must register and account for VAT. A non-established business generally has no general de minimis threshold for French VAT registration when it makes taxable supplies in France, unless a specific reverse-charge or other statutory exception applies. Reduced VAT rates may apply to qualifying food products, but manufactured self-heating meal products require transaction-specific classification and packaging analysis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices, and large and mid-sized businesses must issue domestic B2B electronic invoices and submit required transaction data. From 1 September 2027, small and micro-enterprises must issue domestic B2B electronic invoices. Invoices will generally be exchanged through an approved private platform connected to the public invoicing directory; France is not currently operating a universal real-time pre-clearance model for all VAT invoices. E-reporting applies to specified B2C and cross-border transactions. Electronic invoices must contain required French VAT invoice data, structured or hybrid formats where applicable, and traceability, authenticity, and integrity controls. Export customs declarations remain processed through the French and EU customs systems and are not replaced by the e-invoicing mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may generally qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT under the French rules implementing Article 146 of the EU VAT Directive, provided the exporter can prove exportation and satisfy documentary and timing requirements. The exporter must be the supplier or act through an authorized intermediary, and the goods must physically leave the EU customs territory. Intra-EU supplies may qualify for VAT exemption where the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier retains transport and recapitulative statement evidence. Services supplied to a business established outside France may be outside the scope of French VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rules rather than technically zero-rated; exceptions apply for services connected with French immovable property, admission to events, transport, and other specifically regulated categories. Input VAT refunds require valid purchase invoices, business-purpose evidence, and compliance with the applicable French or EU refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French or EU electronic export customs declaration and export accompanying or exit confirmation evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, Incoterms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, airway bill, road consignment note, or equivalent
Proof of exit from the EU customs territory generated by the customs system or equivalent carrier and customs evidence
Purchase orders, sales contracts, delivery records, and customer or freight-forwarder correspondence linking the goods to the export
Evidence of payment or commercial settlement where relevant; France does not generally require an inward remittance certificate as a condition for export VAT exemption
For intra-EU supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number, transport evidence, and required EC Sales List or recapitulative statement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Export VAT exemption may be denied or retrospectively clawed back if exportation, EU exit, customer status, transport, or transaction substance is not proven. Reassessed VAT is generally payable with late-payment interest, currently calculated under the applicable statutory rate, and may attract a 40% penalty for deliberate non-compliance or an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights; lesser penalties may apply for other procedural failures. False invoices, fabricated customs evidence, or knowingly fraudulent VAT claims may trigger criminal tax-fraud proceedings, administrative fines, customs sanctions, seizure, and liability of responsible officers. Input VAT refunds and related deductions may be disallowed, and assessments may extend to the applicable statutory limitation period, with longer periods or criminal exposure in cases of fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in conjunction with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for balance-of-payments statistical oversight; prudential licensing, AML/CTF enforcement, and banking supervision are exercised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), pursuant to the Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier) and EU Regulation No. 1024/2013 (Single Supervisory Mechanism).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a core Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, which guarantees unrestricted free movement of capital and payments. No exchange-control approval, central-bank clearance, or individual investment license is required for current-account flows, capital subscriptions, loan repayments, or profit remittances. Repatriation of profits is unfettered, subject only to the ordinary corporate income tax (25% standard rate as of 2024), the participation exemption benefits for qualifying subsidiaries, and the 30% withholding tax framework on non-treaty outbound dividends, with treaty relief available under the France-PRC, France-Hong Kong, and France-US DTCs as applicable. Statistical balance-of-payments declarations to the Banque de France are due for cross-border transactions equal to or exceeding EUR 12.5 million per calendar year, and inward direct investments exceeding EUR 15 million held by non-EU investors may be screened under EU Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Regulation 2019/452 and French Decree No. 2019-1590.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender, no statutory repatriation deadline, and no forced conversion ratio into euro. Exporters may retain foreign-currency balances freely in designated foreign-currency accounts held with French-resident banks. The only obligations are statistical: each bank must report to the Banque de France all cross-border settlement flows used for balance-of-payments compilation, with threshold-based declaration of individual payments above EUR 12.5 million per annum and the annual survey of direct investment positions. Trade settlements with counterparties in jurisdictions subject to EU restrictive measures are separately prohibited under the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) framework and EU Regulation 833/2014 as amended.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre) and Operational Account (Compte Courant Professionnel)
Operational Account (Compte Courant) with Global Transaction Banking (GTB) trade-finance module

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (CACIB) / Crédit Agricole S.A.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and FX/Commodity hedging account
Operational Account and Treasury Management Account (Compte Gestion de Trésorerie)
Operational Account and Import/Export Documentary Collections

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for secondary transaction accounts and customer collections; Low for core treasury, capital escrow, and documentary trade operations. EMIs currently active in France operate under PSD2 licenses (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Finom) or under EU passporting rights (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business); they may open corporate accounts through fully remote embedding. However, offshore EMIs domiciled outside the EEA or not passported under PSD2 are legally prohibited from providing payment services in France without an ACPR branch license; their accounts cannot receive share-capital deposits or serve as trust/escrow for the SAS capital injection, and they are unsuitable instruments for LC issuance, cross-border guarantees, or SWIFT-based trade settlement. The SAS should maintain its primary clearing and capital account at a tier-1 ACPR-licensed commercial bank and use fintech EMIs exclusively for collections, expense disbursements, and multi-currency petty treasury accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under ACPR anti-money-laundering guidance implementing the 4th and 5th EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives, remote onboarding is permitted if the bank applies a certified video-identification process with live agent interview, biometric matching, and eIDAS-compliant electronic signature. In practice, BNP Paribas and Société Générale generally mandate an initial physical meeting between the bank's corporate compliance officer and the SAS Président (chief executive) or holder of the individual mandate; some institutions accept remote interview when the corporate signatory is already identified in the bank's database or holds a European Economic Area passport. The registered office address must be evidenced with the French Kbis extract; physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) is routinely waived where the UBO appears in the Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) and provides certified identity documents. The recommended compliance posture is to schedule an in-person meeting of the SAS legal representative at the chosen bank's corporate center in Paris or Lyon within 60 days of incorporation, with remote video verification for all other beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Classification of the product as containing exothermic reaction chemicals (self-heating mechanism), triggering heightened scrutiny under bank's high-risk goods and dual-use screening policy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) and Technical Data Sheets for the exothermic composition; EU CE conformity declarations and food-contact compliance certificates (EU Regulation 1935/2004 and 10/2011); import/export licenses for the chemical precursors; ISO 22000 and HACCP certifications; custody chain contracts showing no involvement of sanctioned entities; UN Manual of Tests and Criteria classification certificates for dangerous goods transport (ADR).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment pattern with large, front-loaded import settlements to suppliers located in mainland China or Hong Kong, combined with high export frequency to non-EU distribution hubs, triggering trade-based money laundering (TBML) indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully stamped commercial invoices; packing lists; original bills of lading and airway bills; certificates of origin; comprehensive import/export customs declarations (DEB/DEN); insurance certificates; signed purchase orders and master supply agreements; bank reference letters from counterparties' banks; customs broker declarations under the Union Customs Code (Regulation 952/2013).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the UBO chain where the SAS is held through a non-EU intermediate holding structure, or where nominee shareholders appear on the corporate register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Kbis extract of the SAS; up-to-date register of beneficial owners (RBE filing receipt from the greffe du tribunal de commerce); chain-of-title chart from ultimate natural persons to the SAS; notarized share subscription deeds; sworn declarations of non-conviction and source of wealth for each UBO; audited financial statements or reference accounts of material shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared low-turnover profile and requested transaction velocity / cross-border volume expected for self-heating meal manufacturing, triggering unusual-activity alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 3-year business plan with volume and margin assumptions; signed shelf-placement contracts or letters of intent with retail distributors; purchase commitments from raw-material suppliers; treasury management forecast showing expected monthly settlement volumes; the bank's Economic Profile Questionnaire (Questionnaire de Profil Économique) completed with exact revenue correlation to bank turnover.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the SAS paid-in capital injection: (i) remitter transfers via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for bank-to-bank cover) to the SAS's euro-denominated IBAN account held at the tier-1 French bank; (ii) the payment must reference the purpose code 'Equity participation / Capital subscription' consistent with the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical classification (chapter D.4 Equity Capital and Investment Fund Shares); (iii) the remitter bank must include the SAS legal name and registered office address to satisfy due-diligence screening; (iv) the SAS must present to its French relationship bank the notarized or counted share-subscription documents, the statutory declaration of subscription and payment (attestation du président), and a capital-deposit certificate where a French bank is used before registration of the SAS at the RCS commercial registry; (v) for injections exceeding EUR 15 million from a non-EU shareholder, an ex-ante FDI screening notification or a Ministerial clearance opinion is required under French Decree No. 2019-1590; and (vi) the beneficiary bank will complete the Banque de France external-transactions reporting (external financial accounts declaration) upon crediting the capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For inbound raw material procurement and outbound finished goods settlement, the SAS will deploy the following clearing rails: (i) euro-denominated settlements inside the single euro payments area (SEPA/SEPA Instant) for EU suppliers and distributors; (ii) cross-border wire transfers via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) and MT202 (bank-to-bank) for non-EU counterparties, with appropriate purpose codes of the Banque de France classification; (iii) confirmed irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit issued under UCP 600 for high-value intermediate purchases (notably self-heating chemical feedstock from mainland China), with reimbursement typically via SWIFT MT700/MT742 and reimbursement claims under URR 725; (iv) documentary collections under URC 522 as a low-cost trade settlement option; and (v) bank payment obligations and trade loans where invoice financing is engaged. All outbound MT103 messages must be pre-screened against the EU consolidated sanctions list, EU asset-freeze listings, and dual-use export control checks under EU Regulation 2021/821, because the exothermic materials used in the final product may trigger dual-use thresholds; end-use attestations from the SAS are therefore mandatory on every wire.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign-exchange forward contracts (deliverable FX forwards) executed with the French relationship bank for euro/renminbi, euro/US-dollar, and euro/pound-sterling payment cycles, with maturity tenors of 1, 3, 6, and 12 months

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to the offshore renminbi (CNH) or any restricted emerging-market currency where physical delivery is not available or prohibited, subject to EMIR margining and trade repository reporting obligations

Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) aligning long-term euro liability streams against renminbi or US-dollar revenue receipts, including mark-to-market collateral arrangements under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and French collateral law (Code Monétaire et Financier Articles L211-38 et seq.)
European-style FX options and zero-cost currency collars (risk reversals) for protecting minimum margin levels on large export invoices while retaining favourable translation participation
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) and tom-next rolling structures to optimize daily liquidity across multiple currency accounts at the tier-1 bank without creating open speculative positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing (Depot des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry, Registre du Commerce et des Societes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within six months after the fiscal year-end; approved financial statements filed with the commercial registry within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, approval is due by 30 June and filing is due by 30 July at the latest.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the company to a court order requiring compulsory filing under a periodic penalty payment ('astreinte') of up to EUR 3,000 per day; persistent non-filing may trigger removal from the RCS, administrative strike-off, and closure of the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaration de resultats, form no. 2065, with 2050-series annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via EDI/EFI electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December financial year-end, by 3 May of the following year; for non-calendar year-ends, by the 3rd day of the second month following the closing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing triggers a penalty of 5% on the assessed corporate income tax, increasing to 10% after 30 days; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month, and tax loss carry-forwards may be rejected until full filing is completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder Decision Approving Annual Accounts (Proces-verbal d'approbation des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory Minute Book (Registre des Decisions de l'Associe - retained internally, not filed with the authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of each financial year-end, and before the annual accounts filing; for a 31 December year-end, the decision must be made by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene and record the annual decision within the statutory period exposes the president/director to a fine of up to EUR 9,000 and a court order compelling the meeting; continued violation may lead to corporate dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Register Update or Year-End Reconciliation (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs - RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (filed in the RCS personal dossier)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership during the year must be filed within 30 days of the change; in every case, the RBE must be accurate and reconciled with the shareholder register before the annual accounts filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate RBE information constitutes a criminal offence punishable by a fine of up to EUR 7,500 and imprisonment for natural persons under Art. L.561-35 of the French Monetary and Financial Code; the company may also be refused copies of RCS extracts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at the balance-sheet date, it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: net balance-sheet assets of EUR 4.0 million, net turnover excluding VAT of EUR 8.0 million, and average workforce of 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies to an SAS that controls one or more subsidiaries or is part of a group structure subject to consolidated accounts, or when minority shareholders holding at least one-third of the capital request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual statutory financial statements are prepared under French GAAP (ANC Regulation 2014-03, Plan Comptable General); consolidated financial statements of listed groups apply IFRS as endorsed by the European Union. Accounts are maintained in euros.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a separate annual RBE confirmation filing. The annual compliance protocol for this SAS therefore consists of: (1) reconciling the RBE with the shareholder register and share-transfer book; (2) identifying any beneficial-owner changes during the fiscal year; (3) if a change occurred, filing the RBE update with the Commercial Court Registry within 30 days of the change; (4) if no change occurred, retaining the existing RBE and certifying its accuracy in the annual accounts filing; and (5) ensuring share transfers are recorded in the statutory books before the annual shareholder decision.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 700 per year for professional domiciliation of a SAS in a business centre or law firm (equivalent to EUR 120 - EUR 600)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 6,000 for a certified statutory audit by a Commissaire aux Comptes for a small-to-mid sized SAS if the audit threshold is triggered; separate expert-comptable compliance assistance fees are additional.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
